newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Wednesday on weak market sentiment, partly triggered by heavy losses on the London Metal Exchange over the past few days, traders said.
The most actively traded October 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 21,950 yuan ($2,647) per tonne, losing 21 yuan from last Friday's close. It opened at 22,050 yuan and hit a high of 22,120.
The market was closed from Saturday to Tuesday to mark the Chinese takeover of Hong Kong, during which time LME copper prices fell, traders said.
July fell 190 to 21,560, August 130 to 21,800, September 180 to 21,900, November 170 to 21,980 and December 210 to 22,000.
Combined volume fell to 30,340 tonnes from 49,710.
Copper opened slightly lower but mostly at their intra-day highs, and fell steadily for most of the session.
Traders said few investors wanted to build positions, which made the contracts continue the slide seen during the last few trading days before the four-day holiday.
"Market sentiment was very weak on Wednesday," said one trader. "Many investors sold in the belief that Shanghai copper has the potential to fall in the short term on the LME losses."
Traders said all contracts closed below the key 22,000-yuan support level today, indicating further falls were likely.

"Such weak prices will frighten away speculators," a second trader said. "The copper contracts will possibly find support at the 21,500 yuan level in the next few days but a major technical rebound seems impossible."
Physical prices in Shanghai are around 21,800 yuan, down from the 22,000 yuan level last week, partly due to successive losses on the futures market, traders said.
Aluminium futures ended up on short-covering.
July rose 10 to 13,600, August 70 to 13,850, September 70 to 14,020, October 120 to 14,170 and November 20 to 14,180.
Combined volume fell to 1,710 tonnes from 3,310.
